newsitem.title: USA: Ford to idle Wixom, Mich., luxury car plant.
newsitem.headline: Ford to idle Wixom, Mich., luxury car plant.

text.p: Ford Motor Co on Thursday said it would suspend production of Lincoln luxury cars at its Wixom, Mich., assembly plant until April 14 because it was scaling back sales to daily rental fleets.

About 2,600 hourly employees at the plant will be affected by the move. The Wixom plant, like all Ford facilities, is not scheduled to operate on Friday or Monday because of the Easter holiday. It will remain idle for the rest of next week and the entire following week, Ford said.
The plant produces a combined total of about 3,900 Lincoln Town Cars, Continentals and Mark VIIIs per five-day week.
Since Ford is cutting back on the number of the cars sold to rental agencies, there were not enough other orders from dealers to keep the plant running.

As of March 1, Lincoln-Mercury dealers had a 79-day supply of Continentals, a 71-day supply of Town Cars and an 87-day supply of Mark VIII coupes, according to industry trade publication Automotive News. Automakers normally consider a 60- to 65-day supply to be ideal.

Despite the downtime at Wixom, Ford said several of its truck plants worked daily overtime this week, including plants in Kansas City and St. Louis, Mo.; Norfolk, Va.; Lorain, Ohio; Oakville, Ont.; and two plants in Louiville, Ky.
